external.description: The U.S. government is planning to acquire a 35% passive stake in Venezuelan businessman Alejandro Betancourt’s North American Blue Energy Partners, according to a report by the Wall Street Journal. This move comes just days after President Donald Trump announced plans to take control of a fifth of Venezuela’s oil reserves. The Pentagon’s Office of Strategic Capital (OSC) intends to structure the investment through penny warrants, allowing the U.S. to gain equity ownership without significant capital outlay. Additionally, the U.S. aims to secure preferential rights to purchase 20% of the company’s production at cost. While the report highlights the potential economic implications of this partnership, Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell clarified that OSC does not take equity stakes in private companies, emphasizing its role as a capital assistance provider through loans or technical support. The White House and Betancourt’s firm have not commented on the matter outside regular business hours. This development underscores ongoing U.S. efforts to influence Venezuela’s oil sector amid geopolitical tensions and economic challenges. Critics argue that such interventions could destabilize regional markets, while proponents see it as a strategic move to secure energy resources. The deal also raises questions about the balance between private enterprise and state control in resource extraction, particularly in politically volatile regions.
